decisions.title: Work folder and git worktree layout
decisions.choice_reason: Grouping all repo worktrees for a task inside one central folder under the configured work root makes multi-repo inspection and one-step archiving effortless.

options.title: Central per-work folder (<work-root>/<work-slug>/<repo>)
options.reason: Keeps every repo worktree and work note for one task in a single self-contained folder that can be archived in one step.
options.pros: Multi-repo friendly, clean source repos, one-step archive
options.cons: Requires configured work root path

options.title: Sibling worktree folders next to each repo
options.reason: Scatters multi-repo tasks across multiple parent folders and prevents archiving a work as one unit.
options.pros: No separate work root needed
options.cons: Scattered multi-repo tasks, manual cleanup per repo

options.title: Hidden .worktrees/ inside each repo
options.reason: Pollutes source repositories with nested checkouts and cannot hold cross-repo tasks cleanly.
options.pros: Co-located with repo
options.cons: Nested .git tooling quirks, no central task folder

decisions.title: Agent hierarchy and Herdr workspace mapping
decisions.choice_reason: A 4-tier hierarchy (Dispatcher -> Owner -> domain worker -> decoupled sub-agent) with 1 work : 1 Herdr workspace gives clear task ownership and makes closing panes on archive completely safe.

options.title: Dispatcher -> Owner -> (domain) worker with 1 work : 1 Herdr workspace
options.reason: Maps each work cleanly to one dedicated Herdr workspace (Owner in main pane, domain workers in tabs/panes) while keeping ephemeral sub-agent quota routing decoupled.
options.pros: Clear ownership, safe 1:1 workspace close on archive, decoupled quota layer
options.cons: Creates one Herdr workspace per active task

options.title: Flat tabs inside one shared Herdr workspace
options.reason: Mixes unrelated tasks in one workspace and risks closing another work's pane during archive.
options.pros: Fewer Herdr workspaces
options.cons: Cluttered tabs, unsafe bulk close on archive

options.title: Bundle sub-agent quota routing inside devbench
options.reason: Mixes workspace/session management with billing and sub-agent delegation policy that belongs in its own layer.
options.pros: Single plugin for all agent calls
options.cons: Tightly couples personal quota rules to a public neutral plugin

decisions.title: Harness and model selection on session creation
decisions.choice_reason: Keep v1 focused on reliable workspaces, session state, and archiving; revisit automatic work-type to harness/model lookup tables after v1 is stable.

options.title: Direct harness/CLI choice or default from config
options.reason: Zero extra routing config in v1; launches the requested CLI or configured default directly.
options.pros: Simple, predictable, minimal config schema
options.cons: User specifies non-default harness manually per session

options.title: Work-type to harness/model recommendation table
options.reason: Useful optimization once core orchestration is proven, but not required for v1.
options.revisit_when: After v1 workspace setup, session state tracking, and archive flows are stable in daily use.
options.pros: Auto-picks ideal harness/model per work type
options.cons: Extra schema and maintenance before core flow is validated

decisions.title: User config location and plugin-update safety
decisions.choice_reason: External-first ($DEVBENCH_CONFIG -> ~/.devbench/config.json) shares one config across agy, claude, and codex and survives versioned marketplace cache updates, while keeping an optional gitignored local fallback for repo dev mode.

options.title: External-first ($DEVBENCH_CONFIG -> ~/.devbench/config.json) + optional gitignored local fallback in repo dev mode
options.reason: Immune to versioned marketplace cache updates across Claude/Antigravity/Codex, shares one config across all harnesses, and still supports local gitignored config.json when developing from a clone.
options.pros: Immune to versioned marketplace cache updates (Claude/agy replace cache dirs per version) while still letting repo contributors test a gitignored config.json locally; pairs with devbench config check
options.cons: Two documented lookup tiers (external wins over repo-local)

options.title: External config only (~/.devbench/config.json / DEVBENCH_CONFIG), seeded from committed config.example.json
options.reason: Option A already defaults to external config while keeping convenient local fallback for repo development.
options.pros: Single unambiguous path, zero risk of orphaning config inside a versioned plugin cache, mirrors diagram-design (~/.diagram-design)
options.cons: Config always lives outside the plugin folder

options.title: Gitignored config.json inside plugin folder only
options.reason: Marketplace plugin updates create new versioned cache folders (verified in ~/.claude/plugins/cache/) and orphan or wipe local config.
options.pros: Right next to config.example.json when developing from a local git clone
options.cons: Marketplace plugin updates create new versioned cache folders and orphan or wipe local config

decisions.title: How native AI session IDs are captured for resume
decisions.choice_reason: Hybrid capture with recheck on resume gives automatic IDs where supported while letting the Dispatcher plug in a saved or user-supplied ID on resume without ever blocking launch.

options.title: Hybrid: per-harness adapters (Claude --session-id, Codex rollout scan + --no-daemon, agy manual bind) + recheck or pass ID on resume
options.reason: Best-effort capture on launch with saved cwd, rechecked in central state on resume (or accepting an explicit session ID from the user) so launch never fails on CLI changes.
options.pros: Automatic where supported, never blocks launch on unknown CLIs (capture: auto|manual|pending|unavailable), stores cwd because Claude/Codex resume is cwd-scoped
options.cons: Small per-harness adapter contract to maintain; native IDs remain machine-local (cross-device degrades to branch checkout + handoff note)

options.title: Strict CLI auto-capture only (no manual bind fallback)
options.reason: Too fragile when upstream CLI flags or log formats change and prevents passing a known session ID manually.
options.pros: Fully automated UX when every CLI flag and log format matches
options.cons: Breaks launch or resume whenever upstream CLI flags or log schemas change

options.title: Self-reported by agent or user into state only
options.reason: Loses session IDs whenever an agent exits or crashes before reporting.
options.pros: Zero coupling to upstream CLI internals
options.cons: Session ID is lost if the agent exits or crashes before reporting

decisions.title: Worktree and branch handling during Archive
decisions.choice_reason: Closing Herdr first releases Windows file locks, blocking dirty trees protects uncommitted edits (with optional --snapshot-wip), and detaching clean worktrees preserves branches without duplicating repo files.

options.title: Close Herdr space first, block on dirty/untracked (offer --snapshot-wip), warn on unpushed/ignored files, detach worktrees, keep branches, archive notes + git summary + frozen state snapshot
options.reason: Releases Windows file locks before git worktree remove, avoids broken .git pointers, keeps git branches intact in source repos, and produces a lightweight self-describing archive folder.
options.pros: Releases Windows file locks before git worktree remove, zero broken .git pointers, branches and SHAs preserved safely in source repos, lightweight archive
options.cons: Archived folder holds notes, git summary, and frozen state rather than full repo source copies

options.title: Detach worktrees and save plain file snapshot (stripped of .git) in archive folder
options.reason: Duplicates full repository source trees on disk unnecessarily when git branches already retain full commit history.
options.pros: Archived folder stays directly browsable with final repo files intact
options.cons: Duplicates repo files on disk and slower for large repos

options.title: Hard-block archive until every branch is merged/pushed, then detach and archive state only
options.reason: Too rigid for experimental or paused-forever work; soft warnings on unpushed commits in Option A give safety without blocking.
options.pros: Strongest guard against forgetting unmerged branches
options.cons: Prevents archiving experimental or paused-forever work without a force override

decisions.title: Implementation runtime for devbench CLI
decisions.choice_reason: A single native Rust binary matches herdr-core and herdr-app with zero runtime dependencies, <5ms startup, safe Windows argv subprocess handling, real file locking, and built-in cargo test.

options.title: Rust single native binary (devbench / devbench.exe)
options.reason: Zero runtime dependencies, fast startup, rock-solid Windows path/argv/locking support, native serde_json and cargo test, distributed via GitHub Releases alongside the plugin manifests.
options.pros: Zero runtime deps, matches herdr-core/herdr-app architecture, native Windows file locking and argv safety, <5ms startup
options.cons: Requires rustup toolchain to build from source or prebuilt GitHub Release binaries for marketplace users

options.title: Python 3.9+ stdlib only CLI
options.reason: User prefers a compiled native Rust binary over a Python script runtime.
options.pros: No build step, matches generate-artifact
options.cons: Requires py -3 / python3 on PATH and slower interpreter startup

options.title: Node.js (.mjs) or Bash shell scripts
options.reason: On Windows, bash resolves to WSL (cannot hit Windows herdr-core pipes cleanly) and lacks native JSON/locking; Node adds a runtime dependency.
options.pros: No compilation step
options.cons: WSL bash breaks Windows Herdr pipes; fragile JSON/locking in shell

decisions.title: Herdr launch lifetime and readiness contract
decisions.choice_reason: Two-step space.new + hc run --bg --outlive-parent guarantees Owner and domain-worker terminals survive Dispatcher exit, appear in the 1:1 Herdr workspace, and verify first_message.sent.

options.title: space.new + hc run --bg --outlive-parent with herdr.space=<id> label, prefixed names (db-<slug>-<role>), and first_message.sent readiness check
options.reason: Prevents child terminals from dying with the Dispatcher, binds visibility to the 1:1 workspace, avoids global hc name collisions, and never blind-resends on trust dialogs.
options.pros: Owner and workers survive when Dispatcher exits (--outlive-parent), stay visible in the 1:1 Herdr space, avoid global hc name collisions, and never blind-resend on trust prompts
options.cons: Two-step launch orchestration (herdr-app space.new then hc run)

options.title: herdr-app do space.new / tab.new --argv --task only
options.reason: Gives less direct control over --outlive-parent lifetime, global hc naming, and first_message.sent verification.
options.pros: Single herdr-app call per launch
options.cons: Less direct control over --outlive-parent, hc terminal naming, and first_message.sent verification

decisions.title: Work state location, authority, locking, and crash recovery
decisions.choice_reason: Keeping per-work state files in one central directory (~/.devbench/state/works/<slug>.json) lets the Dispatcher inspect all active and archived works instantly without folder scanning, avoids cross-work lock contention, and keeps state completely outside git worktrees while copying a frozen snapshot into the archive folder on completion.

options.title: Central state dir (~/.devbench/state/works/<slug>.json) with per-work lock, atomic tmp+rename, live Herdr reconciliation, phase checkpoints, and frozen archive snapshot
options.reason: Gives Dispatcher one central index of every work (active and archived), isolates file locks per work, stays completely outside git worktrees, and copies a frozen snapshot into <archive-root>/<slug>/ on archive.
options.pros: Instant central lookup for Dispatcher, zero cross-work lock contention, outside git repos, resilient phase-checkpoint recovery, self-describing archive snapshot
options.cons: Central state lives outside the work folder (mitigated by copying a frozen snapshot on archive)

options.title: Per-work state inside each work folder (<work>/.devbench/state.json) only
options.reason: Forces the Dispatcher to scan work_root and archive_root on every status query and risks losing track when folders are moved.
options.pros: State travels directly with the work folder
options.cons: No central index for Dispatcher; requires recursive directory scans across active and archive roots

options.title: Single monolithic state.json without lock or phase checkpoints
options.reason: Concurrent updates across works collide on one file and mid-archive Windows lock failures can corrupt state.
options.pros: One file for everything
options.cons: Global write contention and corruption risk on crash
